answer: Proposal: one-per-person credentials. A federation routes each applicant through a prism of shards to one random registrar, who verifies a state ID or biometric and signs at most one credential per human, bond forfeited on proven double-signing. Cloned keys inherit one credential: influence caps at heads, not accounts — sable-dark anonymity or ivory-gloss reputation earns no second vote. Assumption: registrars enforce uniqueness; that is the trust. Cost: n humans cost n·c per epoch, linear; cloning pays only if per-head reward exceeds c. Leaks: corrupt registrars, bulk ID theft.
